candidate.answerReason: Comparing equal-sized groups leaves exactly the group indicated by one of the three balance outcomes. An approximately even three-way split keeps the largest remaining group small.

methods.label: Use a three-way balance search
methods.explanation: Divide the candidates into three groups as evenly as possible, and place two groups containing the same number of items on the two pans. If the balance is level, the lighter item is in the unweighed group. If it is not level, the lighter item is in the group on the higher pan. Continue with that group until one candidate remains.
methods.levelReason: The method is the Grade 5 balance strategy for exactly one exceptional item whose lighter direction is known.

candidate.annotationRationale: The question assesses planning a near-equal three-way split in the known-light model, exactly covered by cnm_p176. The explanation uses equal item counts, handles balanced and unbalanced outcomes, and repeats only within the indicated candidate group. It does not require an unknown-heavy-or-light analysis or a minimum-weighing formula.
